title: Solving the Registered Bank Account Verification Problem in UPI: For Investment Category
summary: Understand TPV in UPI, why payments fail when the bank account does not match, and how investors and broking or mutual fund platforms can prevent wrong-account selection.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


For businesses in mutual funds, broking and investments, registered bank account verification is not a design choice. It is a regulatory requirement.


This check is called[TPV, or Third-Party Validation](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/third-party-validation-feature-for-bfsi-sector-pg/) . SEBI requires investment platforms to accept money only from the bank account the customer registered during onboarding, not from any other account they happen to use. Many NBFCs and lenders apply the same check to tie repayments to the borrower’s own account.


The reason is simple. These sectors are highly exposed to fraud and money laundering, and TPV gives regulators certainty about where the money came from.


##


What Is TPV in UPI and How Does It Work?


TPV in UPI restricts a customer’s payment to one specific, pre-registered bank account. When the merchant creates a payment order, it passes the customer’s registered account number and IFSC. The customer’s bank then checks that the money is coming from that exact account.


TPV works on UPI and net banking, and on bank transfers through IMPS, NEFT and RTGS. The flow is simple in concept:


- The merchant captures and registers the customer’s bank account during onboarding.
- The merchant passes those registered account details when creating the payment order.
- The customer is expected to select the same account in their UPI app at checkout.
- If the customer selects a different account, the transaction fails, but only after PIN entry.


That sequencing, with validation happening after PIN entry rather than before, is where the compliance requirement turns into a business problem.


##


**What Is TPV Failure?**


A TPV failure happens when the bank account used to pay doesn’t match the bank account registered with the investment platform. The bank rejects the payment, and the customer sees a failed transaction, often with no clear reason.


For the customer, it feels like a random UPI error. For the platform, it’s a lost investment at the very last step.


The most common causes:


- **Wrong account selected** : The customer has several accounts linked to their UPI app and taps the default one, which isn’t the registered account.
- **Registered account not linked to the UPI app** : The registered account exists, but the customer never added it to Google Pay, PhonePe or whichever app they’re using.
- **Outdated bank details on the platform** : The customer changed banks or closed the old account but never updated it with the platform.
- **Mismatched details at order creation** : A typo in the account number or[IFSC](https://www.cashfree.com/IFSC-verification-api/) sent by the platform means even the correct account gets rejected.
- **Net banking on an unsupported bank:** For net banking TPV, the customer’s bank has to support validation through the payment gateway.


##


**How to Fix a TPV Failure**


**If you’re an investor:**


- Check which bank account is registered on your investment or trading app. It’s usually under profile or bank details.
- Make sure that same account is linked in your UPI app.
- At the payment screen, switch from your default account to the registered one before entering your PIN.
- If you’ve moved banks, update your bank details on the platform first. Most platforms need to verify the new account before you can pay from it.


**If you run an investment platform:**


- Show customers which account is registered, right on the checkout screen.
- [Validate account number and IFSC at onboarding](https://www.cashfree.com/bank-account-verification/) so bad data never reaches the payment order.
- Let customers register more than one account where your compliance setup allows. Multi-bank TPV can take up to four accounts per order.
- Move validation before PIN entry so the wrong account can’t be chosen at all. More on that below.


##


Wrong Account Selection Problem


Most[UPI apps](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/top-upi-apps-in-india/) display every linked account on the payment screen with no indication of which one is actually permitted. A customer with two or three linked accounts has no way of knowing, at a glance, which one is registered with the merchant. They tap a default account out of habit, enter their UPI PIN, and only then does the transaction fail.


For the customer, this looks like a payment failure they cannot explain.


For the merchant, it is a lost conversion at the final step of checkout, plus the resulting support burden.


This wrong-account selection currently accounts for **8% of total failures** on TPV-enabled merchants.


For businesses processing high transaction volumes daily, this significantly impacts the overall success rate, driven entirely by a UI gap rather than any actual issue with the customer’s intent to pay.


***Also read:[Moving Third Party Validation into the UPI App](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/moving-third-party-validation-into-the-upi-app/)***


##


Our Solution: UPI App TPV


Cashfree has partnered with Google Pay and Paytm to move[TPV validation](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/features/tpv) into the UPI app itself, ahead of PIN entry, rather than relying on backend validation after the fact.


**This is currently a capability unique to Cashfree.**


**With this live:**


**Only registered accounts can be selected:** The customer’s payment screen on Google Pay or Paytm shows only their registered account. If they have more than one registered account, all of them are selectable.


**Every other account is greyed out:** Unregistered accounts can’t be tapped, and they carry a message saying they aren’t registered with the platform.


**Missing accounts get flagged early:** If the registered account isn’t linked on that app yet, the customer is prompted to add it before going any further.


**No integration rework** : Merchants already using Cashfree TPV don’t need to change their existing payment gateway integration.


Because the wrong account is never selectable, the failure is removed at the source instead of being caught and reported afterward.


##


**TPV for Broking and Mutual Fund Platforms**


For stock brokers, mutual fund platforms and bond platforms, TPV isn’t optional. Under SEBI rules, investors must pay only from bank accounts they’ve registered with the platform. A payment from any other account has to be rejected, even if it belongs to the same person.


That makes TPV part of almost every money-in moment on an investment app:


**Use Case** **Typical Payment Mode** **How TPV Applies**


Adding funds to a trading account UPI, net banking Each top-up must come from the registered account


Lump sum mutual fund investment UPI, net banking Payment is validated against the investor’s registered account


SIP and recurring investments[eNACH](https://www.cashfree.com/enach/) ,[UPI AutoPay](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-autopay/) The mandate can only be set up on a verified registered account


Bond and fixed income purchases UPI, net banking, bank transfer Same registered account check as other investments


The compliance side is fixed. What varies is how much the check costs you in failed payments. Investors on these platforms often have two or three bank accounts linked to UPI, and every wrong tap is a failed investment.


When you evaluate a TPV provider, check for:


- **Coverage across modes** : UPI, net banking and recurring mandates should all support TPV, so you don’t run separate flows.
- **Multi-account support** : Investors with more than one registered account shouldn’t be forced to pick one.
- **Validation before PIN entry:** This is the difference between catching a wrong account and preventing it.
- **Clear failure data** : You need to tell a TPV mismatch apart from a[bank decline](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-declined-by-bank-reasons-and-fixes/) , so your support team can guide the investor.


***Also read:[How TPV works with recurring payments for BFSI businesses](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/automating-recurring-payments-with-third-party-validation-why-is-it-a-necessity-for-bfsi-sector/)***

##


**Frequently Asked Questions**


#### **What does TPV stand for in UPI?**


TPV stands for Third-Party Validation. It checks that a UPI or net banking payment comes from the bank account the customer registered with the business.


#### **What is TPV failure?**


A TPV failure means the payment came from a bank account that doesn’t match the one registered with the platform, so the bank rejected it. The most common reason is picking the wrong account in the UPI app.


#### **Why did my UPI payment fail on an investment app even though I have enough balance?**


You may have paid from a bank account that isn’t registered on the app. Investment platforms only accept money from your registered account. Switch to that account in your UPI app and try again.


#### **What does TPV pending mean?**


It means the final status of the payment hasn’t come back from the bank yet. Don’t pay again straight away. Wait for the platform to update the status, as most pending payments resolve on their own.


#### **Is TPV mandatory for mutual fund and broking platforms?**


Yes. SEBI requires platforms dealing in securities, broking and mutual funds to accept investor payments only from registered bank accounts.


#### **Can an investor register more than one bank account for TPV?**


Yes, if the platform allows it. Cashfree supports multi-bank TPV with up to four registered accounts per order, and UPI App TPV shows all of them as selectable.
